newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia introduces special foreign share accounts.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia introduces special foreign share accounts.

text.p: The Slovenian central bank said on Tuesday foreign investors in Slovenian shares must in future hold special trading accounts with fully licensed banks if they wanted to invest in domestic companies.
"In this way we wanted to organise foreign portfolio investment in Slovenia," Darko Bohnec, head of central bank operations, told Reuters.
He said the central bank had notified Slovenian banks of the ruling on Friday. They have 30 days from February 7 to establish the new accounts.
Half of Slovenia's 28 banks have full licenses and will be able to operate the securities accounts. The remainder will no longer be permitted to accept foreign funds for share investment.
Bohnec said the central bank had placed few restrictions on the new trading accounts.
"There are no limits regarding inflow or outflow on these accounts, except when cash transactions are concerned -- those are limited to 250,000 tolars ($1,655) per month," he said.
Among banks with full licenses are four in partial foreign ownership -- SKB bank, Bank Austria, Creditanstalt and Volksbank-Ljudska Banka.
